subject.title: Feature: --agent flag for TUI to select which agent handles the session

question: Should OpenClaw add a native `openclaw tui --agent <id>` startup selector, and what precedence should it have over `--session agent:<id>:...`, cwd workspace inference, remembered sessions, and global session scope?
rationale: This is a new public CLI flag that can change first-turn agent, session, model, provider, auth, and workspace context; source inspection proves the gap but cannot choose the permanent UX contract.

options.title: Add the startup flag
options.body: Implement an additive `--agent <id>` flag with explicit precedence rules and tests for session keys, cwd inference, remembered sessions, global scope, model/provider routing, and docs.

options.title: Keep current workarounds
options.body: Document agent-scoped session keys, workspace inference, and `/agent <id>` as the supported paths, accepting that arbitrary-directory startup remains less ergonomic.

options.title: Defer to a broader TUI routing design
options.body: Leave this open until maintainers settle a larger startup/session/model-routing contract for TUI and related clients.

recommendation.title: Add the startup flag
recommendation.body: Implement an additive `--agent <id>` flag with explicit precedence rules and tests for session keys, cwd inference, remembered sessions, global scope, model/provider routing, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent review/context trail for this exact TUI startup gap and current TUI CLI/runtime blame in the available checkout.
